Welcome
Hello and Welcome to our school website. Hiltingbury Junior School is a friendly learning community which seeks to provide an inclusive education for all of our pupils. The twelve classes (three per year group) are housed in spacious, well-resourced classrooms, served by a large staff of dedicated teachers and teaching assistants.

P.E and Sports Premium
About the PE and Sports Premium:
All young people should have the opportunity to live healthy and active lives. A positive experience of sport and physical activity at a young age can build a lifetime habit of participation and is central to meeting the government’s ambitions for a world-class education system.
Physical activity has numerous benefits for children and young people’s physical health, as well as their mental wellbeing (increasing self-esteem and emotional wellbeing and lowering anxiety and depression), and children who are physically active are happier, more resilient and more trusting of their peers. Ensuring that pupils have access to sufficient daily activity can also have wider benefits for pupils and schools, improving behaviour as well as enhancing academic achievement.
The School Sport and Activity Action Plan set out government’s commitment to ensuring that children and young people have access to at least 60 minutes of sport and physical activity per day, with a recommendation of 30 minutes of this delivered during the school day (in line with the Chief Medical Officers guidelines which recommend an average of at least 60 minutes per day across the week).
The PE and sport premium can help primary schools to achieve this aim, providing primary schools with £320m of government funding to make additional and sustainable improvements to the quality of the PE, physical activity and sport offered through their core budgets. It is allocated directly to schools so they have the flexibility to use it in the way that works best for their pupils. The PE and sport premium survey highlighted the significant impact which PE and Sport has had in many primary schools across England.

Our School Vision, Values & Ethos
"Learning, Caring and Achieving Together"
Our school vision, values and ethos
Our school community values are unique to our school as they have been chosen by parents, staff, governors and children. We all believe that these values will support the personal, social and emotional development of every child in our school. We also believe that through working in partnership with the school community we share the responsibility together in supporting each child.
Respectfulness means being considerate and thinking of yourself, others and the environment. This includes respecting beliefs and treating everyone with kindness.'
Kindness is a chain reaction – when people are kind to us, we feel encouraged to be kind to others. Kindness is helping and taking care of others – treating people the way we want to be treated ourselves.
Honesty means being truthful to yourself and others about things you have done. This also includes how you are feeling about situations, which can be hard to do.
Equality means that everybody is treated fairly, and that we embrace and celebrate our differences at Hiltingbury, in our community and across the world.
Building our resilience means being aware of strong emotions so that we are better protected in the face of smaller, everyday incidents, and better able to withstand, manage, and recover from difficult situations. To help us be resilient, we use good problem-solving skills, we build independence and have the courage to ask for help when we need it.
We strive to share, encourage and model our values with our children to prepare and support their development at Hiltingbury and for their future.

Our Learning Values
Here at Hiltingbury, our passion for developing the learning skills of our children is at the very heart of our curriculum. This ethos is embedded throughout the school and is reflected in the positive and passionate learning behaviours that our children display. Each and every member of our dedicated teaching team believe in and drive our ‘WECARE’ learning values, which are carefully nurtured throughout our children’s journeys at Hiltingbury.
WE CARE Learning Skills
Working Together, Enthusiasm, Creativity, Ambition, Reflection and Enquiry
It is these positive and inspiring learning values that provide our children with the foundations they need to succeed: ensuring that each child embraces challenge and develops the desire to grow as learners. Our inclusive culture means that every child is supported to do this, nurturing their self-belief and determination to make strong progress.
The commitment of our staff, to care for and provide the best possible education for our pupils, shows no limits.
This, along with the support of our parents, makes us all proud to be members of the Hiltingbury community, where we believe that every child can and will fulfil their potential.

Reporting your child's absence
Absence Procedure
We understand that children will be unwell sometimes. If your child is not well enough to come to school, please complete the google form below. We would ask that all absences are reported by 8.40am at the latest.
To report your child's absence please complete this linked google form
Is my child too ill for school - Please click this link to the NHS website page for guidance on whether to send your child to school.
Requests for holiday leave in term time cannot be authorised. Please refer to our Attendance page for information and access to the application form requesting absence due to exceptional circumstances.
We keep you informed of your child’s attendance on a termly basis and work with families in times of difficulty to continue to promote good attendance.

Clubs & Activities
At Hiltingbury Junior School, we believe in the importance of a well-rounded education, and our extracurricular after-school clubs are designed to support our pupils’ growth in a variety of areas beyond the classroom. These clubs offer a fantastic opportunity for children to discover new hobbies, build their confidence, and develop important life skills in a safe and engaging environment.
We are proud to offer a wide range of after-school clubs catering to different interests and age groups. Whether your child is interested in sports, the arts, or music, there’s something for everyone!
We are delighted to offer support to those families in receipt of Free Schools Meals. If your child is in receipt of free school meals, there will be the option to sign up for one club under their pupil premium funding.
Bookings are made via your child's Arbor accoung. For your Arbor "How to" please click this link: Signing my child up for a Club on the Parent Portal or Arbor App.
If you need any assistance, please contact our friendly office team.
For further details of our Charging & Remissions Policy, please refer to our policy tab.
